cls: Selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) - estrogen agonist/antagonist
pharm: SERM that acts as an estrogen agonist in bone (reducing resorption) and an antagonist in breast and uterine tissue, used for osteoporosis and breast-cancer risk reduction.
quick: Take any time of day, with or without food
Not for use in nursing women
Use with caution; limited data in significant impairment
Use with caution; not studied adequately in impairment
No specific interaction; moderate use reasonable
Signs of VTE, triglycerides if prior estrogen-related elevation, bone density
summary: Raloxifene is a selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) indicated for the treatment and prevention of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women and for reducing the risk of invasive breast cancer in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis or at high risk. The dose is one 60 mg tablet once daily, with calcium and vitamin D supplementation as needed. It carries a BOXED WARNING for increased risk of venous thromboembolism (DVT/PE) and death from stroke in women with or at risk for coronary heart disease. It is contraindicated in active or prior VTE and in pregnancy, and should be stopped 72 hours before and during prolonged immobilization.
indications: Treatment and prevention of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women
Reduction in the risk of invasive breast cancer in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis
Reduction in the risk of invasive breast cancer in postmenopausal women at high risk for invasive breast cancer

dosage.n: Add calcium and/or vitamin D if dietary intake is inadequate
Optimum duration of treatment not established

admin: Take one 60 mg tablet orally once daily at any time of day, with or without food
Ensure adequate calcium (postmenopausal women ~1500 mg/day elemental) and vitamin D (400-800 IU/day)
Discontinue at least 72 hours before and during prolonged immobilization (e.g., surgery, long travel); resume only when fully mobile
Not for use to treat existing invasive breast cancer or prevent recurrence
moa: Raloxifene is an estrogen agonist/antagonist (SERM) whose actions are mediated through binding to estrogen receptors, activating estrogenic pathways in some tissues and blocking them in others depending on coactivator/corepressor recruitment. In bone it acts as an estrogen agonist, decreasing bone resorption and turnover, increasing bone mineral density, and reducing fracture incidence. In uterine and breast tissue it acts as an estrogen antagonist, lacking estrogen-like stimulation and reducing the risk of estrogen-receptor-positive invasive breast cancer.

absolute: Active or past history of venous thromboembolism (deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, retinal vein thrombosis)
Women who are or may become pregnant
relative: Increased risk of stroke (e.g., documented CHD or major coronary risk)
monitor: Serum triglycerides if prior estrogen-related elevation

preg: Raloxifene is contraindicated in pregnancy because it may cause fetal harm. Women who are or may become pregnant should not use raloxifene.
lact: Raloxifene should not be used by nursing women; it is not known whether it is excreted in human milk, and it may pass into milk with potential effects on the infant.
renal: Use with caution in patients with renal impairment; raloxifene has not been adequately studied in moderate-to-severe renal impairment.
hepatic: Use with caution in patients with hepatic impairment; raloxifene plasma concentrations correlate with the degree of impairment and safety/efficacy have not been adequately established.

major: Cholestyramine (and other anion exchange resins) - significantly reduces raloxifene absorption; do not co-administer
Systemic estrogens - concomitant use is not recommended
Warfarin and other coumarin anticoagulants - raloxifene can modestly decrease prothrombin time; monitor INR
moderate: Highly protein-bound drugs (e.g., diazepam, lidocaine) - theoretical displacement; monitor
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.diagnostics: May lower total cholesterol and LDL; monitor triglycerides in women with prior estrogen-induced hypertriglyceridemia.

serious: Venous thromboembolism (deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, retinal vein thrombosis)
Increased risk of death from stroke in women with/at risk for coronary heart disease
rare: Hypertriglyceridemia (in women with prior estrogen-induced elevation)

monitoring: Signs and symptoms of venous thromboembolism
Bone mineral density to assess osteoporosis response
Serum triglycerides in women with prior estrogen-induced hypertriglyceridemia
Stroke risk factors in women with coronary heart disease
counsel: Take one tablet daily at any time, with or without food, and take calcium and vitamin D as advised
Stop the medicine and call your doctor about 3 days before, and during, any prolonged immobilization such as surgery or long trips
Seek urgent care for leg pain/swelling, sudden chest pain or shortness of breath, or sudden weakness/vision or speech changes
Do not use if you are or could become pregnant
Hot flashes and leg cramps are common; report severe or persistent symptoms
pk: Reduction in bone turnover develops over weeks; effects build over months
Once-daily dosing maintains effect; bone benefits accrue with continued use
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); excursions permitted 15-30 C (59-86 F)
pearls: BOXED WARNING: increased risk of venous thromboembolism (DVT/PE) and death from stroke in women with or at risk for coronary heart disease
Contraindicated in active or prior VTE and in pregnancy
Discontinue 72 hours before and during prolonged immobilization to reduce clot risk
SERM: estrogen agonist in bone (anti-resorptive), antagonist in breast/uterus (does not stimulate endometrium, reduces ER+ breast cancer)
Not for primary or secondary prevention of cardiovascular disease; cholestyramine markedly reduces absorption
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the once-daily schedule. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: There is limited experience with raloxifene overdose. In adults, doses well above the recommended dose have been tolerated; reported symptoms with intentional overdose include leg cramps and dizziness. There is no specific antidote; treatment is supportive.
